final_candidates.decision_summary: Highest EVEscape score (0.964) with the best PLM plausibility (0.378) among top escape candidates, in the Sa/Ca antigenic region; structure not applicable, so no structural red flag.
Strong escape (0.881) with neutral-to-beneficial PLM (1.0), the best replication-fitness proxy in the pool; located in the Ca antigenic site.
High escape (0.877) with acceptable structure compatibility (0.588); low PLM is a fitness concern but classic antigenic-site charge reversals often remain viable.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 ranking is stable across escape, plausibility, and structure dimensions; additional evidence unlikely to change the decision.

history.rationale: Position 157 lies in the Sa antigenic site; charge-reversal mutations here are classic antibody escape changes in H1 HA while remaining surface-exposed and structurally tolerated.
Charge-reversing Lys->Glu in the Sa antigenic region is a classic escape motif with minimal structural disruption; pending phenotype/EVEscape confirmation.
Highest EVEscape (0.964) with the best PLM plausibility (0.378) among the top escape candidates; structure is n/a due to WT mismatch, so no structural red flag either.
Residue 158 is in the immunodominant Sa loop; a hydrophobic substitution disrupts antibody recognition with minimal impact on the fold.
Adjacent to K157 in the Sa site; side-chain change can disrupt antibody binding while surface-exposed loop tolerates variation.
Escape (0.773) and structure (0.744) are decent but near-zero PLM (0.006) raises a replication-fitness concern; demoted.
Position 186 is in the Sb antigenic site near the 190-helix; introducing a charged residue can abolish Sb-directed antibody binding.
Gly->Glu introduces a bulky charged side chain in the Sb site, likely disrupting antibodies but with higher folding risk; keep as mid-confidence.
Escape is high (0.892) but structure (0.467) and PLM (0.045) both suggest fitness cost, keeping it just below K187E.
Sb-site charge reversal at 187 is a well-documented escape mechanism; surface location preserves folding and receptor function.
Charge reversal in the Sb antigenic region; strong escape candidate with moderate fitness risk to be checked via structure/plm.
High escape (0.877) with acceptable structure compatibility (0.588); low PLM (0.01) is a fitness concern but classic antigenic-site Lys-to-Glu changes often score low in PLM yet remain viable.
Charge swap at Sb residue 188 alters the local electrostatic epitope; conservative volume change limits structural disruption.
Reverse charge swap at Sb site; complementary hypothesis to K187E/G186E in same epitope patch.
Moderate escape (0.751) with excellent structure compatibility (0.876); a safe fallback if fitness dominates.
Position 169 is in the Ca antigenic site (Ca2 loop); escape variants at 169-173 are known in H1 evolution.
Surface Lys->Glu near the Sa/Ca junction; plausible escape with low structural cost.
Second-highest escape (0.941) but the worst structure compatibility (0.249) and near-zero PLM indicate likely replication-fitness damage; demoted.
Ca-site residue 172; loss of negative charge can reduce antibody binding while Asn is sterically similar.
Asp->Asn is a conservative change that may remove an epitope contact; lower escape magnitude than charge reversals, so ranked below charge-swap candidates.
Strong escape (0.881) combined with a perfect PLM ratio (1.0, neutral-to-beneficial), the best replication-fitness proxy in the pool; structure unavailable, so promoted to rank 2.
Ca1-site residue 224 is surface-exposed; neutralizing the positive charge may evade Ca-directed antibodies with modest fitness cost.
Ca-site surface Arg->Gln, conservative; escape benefit uncertain but low fitness risk.
Best structure (0.958) and decent PLM (0.311) but escape (0.637) is below the leading cluster.
Conservative aromatic change at Sa-loop residue 161 can subtly alter epitope geometry while retaining near-wild-type fitness.
Tyr->Phe is highly conservative and likely weak for escape; downgraded relative to charge-changing candidates.
Lowest escape (0.477) with mediocre structure and PLM; no path to the Top-3.

rejection.reason: Lowest escape (0.477) with mediocre structure and PLM; no path to the Top-3.

history.rationale: Sb-site residue 197; removing the histidine charge can perturb antibody recognition near the 190-helix.
His->Asn at a surface position; possible glycan-free epitope alteration, kept at moderate-low confidence pending evidence.
Low escape (0.557) plus near-zero PLM; dominated by better candidates.
